clue.text: Latvian's yarn about Dracula's home

indicators.note: 'about' can mean around and in disorder, so the letters are tumbled into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the possessive supplies its S as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A storyteller from Latvia spins a tale about the vampire's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S in Latvian's is not grammar here: its S is needed in the fodder alongside the four letters of yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's novel places the count's castle in this region of Romania, so it is the vampire's homeland.

clue.text: Prompt to accommodate a rest

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to a guest, so one piece houses another inside it

parts.note: a prompt is something that jogs the memory
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cue telling someone to take a short break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' reads as a verb or adjective, but it is a noun meaning a reminder, which then takes in the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is whatever is left over, which is exactly what a leftover portion or balance is.

clue.text: Ten set up formal party game

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Ten guests organise a party game at a formal do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party game' looks like the definition together, but 'party' belongs to the wordplay and only 'game' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, related to basketball, played widely in Britain and Commonwealth countries.

clue.text: New York baseball player to tug lever regularly

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, a tug

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A ballplayer from New York is told to pull a lever repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' seems to describe how often the lever is tugged, but it picks alternate letters from 'lever'.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York Yankees are a Major League Baseball team, so any member of the squad is called by its singular name.

clue.text: Essential small bottle contains last of reagent

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a vial is a little glass bottle

indicators.note: 'last of' points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lab note: the key vial holds the last drops of a chemical reagent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' looks like an adjective for the bottle, but it is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is absolutely necessary, and vital carries that same sense of indispensable importance.

clue.text: Criticise turning up for snooze

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means flipping to read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pan a film or play is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for arriving to take a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' suggests arriving, but in a down clue it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooze is a short light sleep, the same thing as a brief doze during the day.

clue.text: Tally is five good marks — capital!

parts.note: to tally is to add up
taken as written
five good grades in a row, alternating top marks A and B

explanation.surface: A school report: five good grades, which is splendid!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' reads as an old-fashioned exclamation of approval, but it defines a capital city. The five marks are school grades, A and B alternating.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia and seat of the African Union.

clue.text: Release what prisoners do in retirement

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: prisoners do time, i.e. serve their sentence

explanation.surface: Talk of freeing inmates and what convicts get up to once they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' sits naturally with prisoners, but it is the definition; the prison phrase 'do time' supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, as a light or gas is released into the air.

clue.text: Depot an awful place to write

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a warehouse is a miserable spot to do one's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful place' looks like a single phrase about the depot, but 'awful' works on the letters before it and 'place to write' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of paper sheets used for jotting things down.

clue.text: After second drink, pledge tracksuit perhaps

indicators.note: 'after' places one item later in the line than the others named

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
port is a fortified wine
to swear is to vow or pledge

explanation.surface: After another drink, someone promises to wear a tracksuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second drink' suggests a refill, but 'second' gives its abbreviation and 'drink' is port.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is one example of athletic clothing, hence the 'perhaps' marking an instance of a broader category.

clue.text: Prepare to grab at ape, say

indicators.note: grabbing takes hold of something, so one piece clasps another inside it

parts.note: to prime is to make ready
taken as written

explanation.surface: Get ready to snatch at a gorilla, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the ape as one example of the class, so the answer is the wider group.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes belong to the mammal order that also includes monkeys and humans, so an ape is one example.

clue.text: Sussex town featured in terrible western

indicators.note: something featured in a film appears inside it, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An English town shows up in a dreadful cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county on England's south coast; Lewes is its county town, known for bonfire night celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a historic market town in East Sussex, England, so it fits the place description.

clue.text: Hound twin developing murder mystery

indicators.note: developing means changing form over time, so these letters grow into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog's twin sibling is working on a detective novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' suggests the Baskervilles, a real murder mystery, but it is simply anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story where readers try to guess the killer, a common name for a crime puzzle novel.

clue.text: Led astray following free puzzle

indicators.note: 'following' places one piece after the other in the line

parts.note: to rid is to free of something

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters drift into another order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone misled into thinking a puzzle is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led astray' reads as one phrase meaning deceived, but 'Led' is fodder and 'astray' scrambles it, placed after the word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a question or problem posed as a brainteaser, so it is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Bury some linen Tom bought

indicators.note: 'some' means only a portion, so the letters are a part taken from within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Instruction to bury a few sheets that Tom purchased.
explanation.walkthrough: The linen suggests a shroud, which fits the burial picture nicely while hiding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb or grave, which is to bury it.

clue.text: Reportedly recognises one who suffered operation

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so sound matters more than spelling

parts.note: to recognise someone is to know them
the biblical Job, famous for his patient suffering, said with a long O

explanation.surface: Word is that someone recognises a patient who went through surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical Job is pronounced with a long O, unlike job meaning work, yet the spellings match; only the first word changes spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose, is informally called by this name, so it is an operation.

clue.text: Newspaper employee rioted unfortunately

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper staffer sadly took part in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rioted' reads as the employee's action, but it is the raw material for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the journalist who oversees and corrects copy at a paper, so a staff member there.

clue.text: Cancel vigorous clean

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to call off a plan, as in informal usage
second meaning: a hard rubbing wash with a brush

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vigorous clean' reads as a noun phrase, and the answer works as a noun there; 'Cancel' takes the verb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to abandon or call off an event informally and a thorough brushing wash of a surface.

clue.text: Contests objections involving nothing

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or take in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: as in 'no ifs or buts', buts are objections
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: Disputes where people raise objections about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contests' could be a verb meaning disputes, chiming with objections, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouts are boxing or wrestling matches, individual fights between opponents, so they are contests.

clue.text: Interrupt detectives beginning to relax in bath

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors in British police ranks

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside another

parts.note: a tub is a bathtub

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Police barge in just as someone starts to unwind in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the British abbreviation for a Detective Inspector, so detectives are DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt someone is to break into their peace, the same as bothering or intruding on them.

clue.text: Tire out smoker at back of vehicle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wear someone out completely
second meaning: the pipe at a car's rear that puffs out fumes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tire' looks like a car tyre in North American spelling, tying it to the vehicle, but it means fatigue. A smoker is normally a person, here the pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for draining all energy and a noun for the tailpipe that expels engine gases.

clue.text: Concealed greeting card finally

parts.note: hi is an informal hello

indicators.note: 'finally' means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A greetings card was eventually tucked out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greeting card' reads as one item, but the two words split: 'greeting' gives the hello and 'card' gives only its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealed and the answer are both past tenses meaning kept out of view or put somewhere secret.

clue.text: Curse jazz improvisation needing xylophone primarily

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A jazz musician curses a solo that needs a xylophone above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' seems to belong to xylophone alone, but it applies to all four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a spell of bad luck laid on someone, so it serves as a synonym for a hex or curse.

clue.text: Again share out wine before one small testimonial

indicators.note: 'before' puts the first item ahead of the rest in the line

parts.note: red is red wine
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a testimonial is a tribute paid in someone's honour

explanation.surface: Pass round the wine once more ahead of a modest farewell tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share out wine' looks like a single action, but 'Again share out' is the definition and the wine starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To redistribute is to hand out or allocate once more, the prefix re- supplying the sense of repetition.
